# Rate-matrix scaling

Scaling assigns a biological unit to every phylogenetic branch. PalantiR
supports two distinct synonymous units, and code should name the intended one
explicitly whenever the distinction matters.

| Constructor input | Stored value | Meaning of one branch-length unit |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `"synonymous"`, `"dS"`, or `"ds"` | `"dS"` | One neutral synonymous substitution per synonymous opportunity, equivalent to one neutral nucleotide substitution per site |
| `"synonymous-per-codon"` | `"synonymous-per-codon"` | One expected synonymous event per codon at stationarity |
| `"non-synonymous"` | `"non-synonymous"` | One expected amino-acid-changing event per codon at stationarity |
| `"standard"` or `"substitution"` | `"substitution"` | One expected substitution of any kind per codon at stationarity |
| `"none"` | `"none"` | No rate normalization |

Since version 1.3.0, `scaling_type = "synonymous"` selects the dS gauge.
Earlier PalantiR releases used that name for the event-count-per-codon gauge;
that historical behavior remains available as `"synonymous-per-codon"`.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
use_genetic_code("Standard nuclear")
MutationSelection(..., scaling_type = "synonymous")            # dS
MutationSelection(..., scaling_type = "synonymous-per-codon")  # event count
```

# The dS gauge

## GY94

For GY94, PalantiR constructs the neutral generator
\(\widetilde Q^{(1)}\) by setting \(\omega=1\). If \(\pi\) is its stationary
codon distribution, its total neutral rate is

$$
r_{\mathrm{tot}}^{(1)} =
  \sum_i \pi_i \sum_{j\ne i}\widetilde q_{ij}^{(1)}.
$$

PalantiR divides the selected generator by
\(S_{dS}=r_{\mathrm{tot}}^{(1)}/3\). The neutral reference consequently has
three substitutions per codon per dS unit, or one per nucleotide site. This
denominator is independent of the selected \(\omega\).

Let \(N_S\) be the stationary synonymous flux of this dS-scaled neutral
reference. On a stationary branch of length \(D\), the expected synonymous
count across \(n\) codon sites is

$$
E[C_S] = nN_SD.
$$

Thus histories recover the branch length as
\(\widehat D=C_S/(nN_S)\), rather than as synonymous events per codon.
For the same neutral reference, the expected nonsynonymous count under GY94 is
\(E[C_A]=n\omega N_A D\), which gives the usual opportunity-corrected dN/dS.

## Mutation--selection models

For mutation--selection models, PalantiR builds a mutation-only neutral
reference by removing amino-acid fitness differences. All fitness profiles
derived from the same nucleotide mutation model therefore share one neutral
clock. A selected profile is not renormalized by its realized synonymous flux,
which can change with codon composition or selection.

The model object reports `neutral_total_rate`, `neutral_synonymous_rate`, and
`synonymous_opportunities`. The last quantity is \(N_S\), the expected number
of synonymous opportunities per codon per dS unit under the neutral reference.
It also stores a per-state vector, `dS_outflux`, for time-heterogeneous
rescaling. The canonical value recorded in `model$scaling_type` is `"dS"`.

# Event-count gauges

For an event class \(\mathcal A\), PalantiR computes the stationary flux

$$
S_{\mathcal A}(Q,\pi)=
  \sum_i\pi_i\sum_{j\ne i}q_{ij}
  \mathbf 1\{i\rightarrow j\in\mathcal A\}.
$$

Dividing \(Q\) by this flux makes a stationary branch of length one carry one
expected event in \(\mathcal A\) per codon. This definition gives the
`"synonymous-per-codon"`, `"non-synonymous"`, and `"substitution"` gauges.
It is an event budget, rather than an opportunity-corrected evolutionary
distance.

# Time-heterogeneous branches

When a fitness profile, population size, or other model parameter changes on
a branch, the inherited codon distribution is generally not stationary under
the new generator. PalantiR therefore integrates the requested branch-length
currency along the transient; it does not assume the destination model starts
at equilibrium.

For dS, let \(Q^0_{dS}\) be the neutral reference expressed in dS units and

$$
h_i^{dS}=\frac{1}{3}\sum_{j\ne i}(Q^0_{dS})_{ij}.
$$

If the selected process enters the branch with distribution \(p_0\) and runs
for intrinsic time \(\tau\), the exact rescaler chooses \(\tau\) so that

$$
\int_0^\tau p_0^T e^{Qu}h^{dS}\,du
=D\,(\pi_{\mathrm{dest}}^T h^{dS}),
$$

where \(D\) is the supplied branch length and \(\pi_{\mathrm{dest}}\) is the
destination model's equilibrium distribution. The selected generator \(Q\)
still controls the substitution history; the neutral functional supplies only
the clock used for the scalar time change. Consequently, dS scaling preserves
neutral nucleotide time through a fitness or population-size shift without
forcing one realized synonymous event per codon. Event-count gauges use the
corresponding selected event-class outflux instead. See
[Temporal Heterogeneity Rescaling](Temporal_Heterogeneity_Rescaling.html) for
the numerical implementation.

# Choosing a gauge

Use dS scaling when tree lengths represent neutral nucleotide substitutions
per site, including lengths estimated from noncoding sequence or fourfold
degenerate positions, or when a branch or branch-site test is meant to compare
nonsynonymous change against a fixed synonymous distance. Use
`"synonymous-per-codon"` only when the desired input is a stationary expected
number of synonymous events per codon. Use `"substitution"` or
`"non-synonymous"` when the corresponding event count is the intended clock.

These gauges are not numerically interchangeable. At stationarity,

$$
Q_{dS}=N_SQ_{\mathrm{syn/codon}},
\qquad
D=\frac{C_S}{nN_S}.
$$

The [engine-validation report](engine_validation.html) tests both synonymous
definitions directly, including GY94 and mutation--selection dS branches.
